messages:
harper: hey everyone, just unboxed my MacBook Pro 14 (M1) and went through setup assistant — didn't see any "Remote Management" or MDM prompt, it just went to Create a Computer Account. do i need to do something special?

it-bot: New device check: serial pending ABM assignment. Logged as harper-device-1772008888.

itops: welcome harper! that usually means the device isn't assigned to our Apple Business Manager (ABM) deployment profile. can you share the serial? either About this Mac -> Serial Number or run:

```bash
system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | awk -F': ' '/Serial/ {print $2}'
```

harper: serial is C02ZQ0ABCDE. pasted here from the sticker too.

nina: checking ABM... hmm the serial exists but it's in the 'unassigned' pool (likely vendor didn't map it). i'll reassign it to the "Redwood Automated Enroll" profile and trigger a remote erase. give me ~5m.

leo: quick note about Activation Lock: if you used a personal Apple ID during initial setup the device could be Activation Locked. if Setup Assistant asks for the Apple ID that's the lock. best to avoid signing in with personal Apple ID until after enrollment, but we can remove it if needed.

harper: ah i did sign in with my personal iCloud because i wanted my photos, sorry 😅. if Activation Lock pops up, what should I do?

leo: sign out isn't possible from Setup Assistant. if Activation Lock appears you'll need to sign in with that Apple ID to proceed, or we can request Apple remove the lock (they usually ask for proof of purchase). first let's see if reassign+erase fixes it — sometimes the wipe clears the temporary state.

nina: ok i've reassigned the serial in ABM and sent a remote erase command. you should see a message on the Mac that a remote erase was initiated. after the erase completes, the Setup Assistant should show a "Remote Management" / "Redwood Enrollment" screen instead of Create an Account. if not, you'll need to manually erase: Settings -> General -> Transfer or Reset -> Erase All Content and Settings (or in Recovery: Options -> Erase Mac).

it-bot: ABM update: serial C02ZQ0ABCDE assigned to Redwood Automated Enroll. Remote erase command issued.

harper: i got the remote erase notification, it's erasing now. thanks!

nina: once it reboots, connect to Redwood-Secure and the automated enrollment profile should appear. if it doesn't, reboot into recovery and erase manually. here are commands to grab serial from Recovery if needed:

```bash
# in Terminal from Recovery
system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep "Serial Number"
```

harper: post-erase, i'm back at Setup Assistant and now i see "This Mac is managed by Redwood Inference" — yay. tapped next and it asked to join network and then did enrollment.

it-bot: Enrollment complete for device-1772008888. Profile: Redwood MDM (supervised). FileVault policy pending.

leo: good. FileVault will be applied automatically and the recovery key stored in MDM. i'll also add you to the temporary admin group for installs. if you need Rosetta for any x86 tooling, run:

```bash
/usr/sbin/softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license
```

harper: installed Rosetta and Homebrew working now. one question — how long is the temporary admin access?

nina: we grant temporary admin for 7 days by default to install dev tools, then we revoke. open a support ticket if you need an extension.

harper: perfect, that covers it. thanks for the quick turnaround and help with ABM assignment :pray: 

leo: welcome! we'll add a short note to the new-hires checklist to verify ABM assignment before unboxing next time to avoid the extra step.

it-bot: Note added to onboarding checklist (task created for devex).
